title: Look-ahead bias is the sneaky bug that turns a mediocre strategy into a backtest genius
author: socialwhizca
selftext:
This one cost me weeks because it's invisible until you go looking. Look-ahead bias is when your backtest accidentally uses information that wouldn't have been available at decision time, and it inflates results in ways that feel real. The classic version is using a bar's close to make a decision you'd act on during that same bar, or an indicator that repaints, or the day's high before the day finished.



The tell is a backtest that looks too clean, especially an equity curve with almost no drawdown. If live is wildly worse than backtest and it's not slippage or costs, look-ahead is a prime suspect, because it's a bug that only exists in the past-data environment and vanishes the moment you go live.



The fix is being paranoid about time, only letting a decision use data that was fully closed and available at that timestamp, and forward-testing on unseen data before trusting anything. My own live gap shrank once I stopped assuming perfect fills too, running live on AvaTrade the intraday spread was nothing like my flat assumption, but look-ahead was the bigger silent killer. What's the sneakiest source of it you've caught in your own code?

comments.author: CODE_HEIST
comments.body:
one test i'd add is to cut the dataset at a historical decision time and recompute the signal. it should match the signal for that time when the later rows are present. if adding future rows changes an earlier decision, there's something to investigate.

i'd run that against feature preparation too, not just the entry code. fitting a scaler on the whole dataset can leak information without a single obvious future-price reference in the strategy.
